messages:
Marta: Quick heads-up — we want to run a small canary that increases the reserved-rate for high-usage dev accounts by 5% next week. Need ops + billing signoff.
Ashwin: Thanks — can you outline the safety checks you want?
Marta: Main goals: make sure invoice previews match realtime usage, ensure grandfathered customers aren’t auto-migrated, and validate meter reconciliation for burst credits.
Ryan: On grandfathering: which cohort exactly? we have ~120 customers flagged as ‘legacy-v1’ that should be excluded.
Marta: Yes, exclude legacy-v1. Also exclude any account with active committed-reserved contracts.
Dana: Who will run the invoice-preview? I can run a dry-run export against last 30 days.
Marta: That would be great. Please run for a random sample of 50 accounts (mix of small/med/large).
Dana: Will do. ETA end of day tomorrow.
Ashwin: For reconciliation: I’ll deploy a quick diff job that compares meter-exports to billing-aggregates and emits anomalies >0.5% variance. I’ll post results here.
Marta: Nice — also want a threshold for abort: if more than 3 anomalies in the sample, we hold the canary.
Ryan: Sounds reasonable. Also we need an ops rollback window — how long after canary start do we watch?
Marta: 48 hours with hourly checks for the first 6 hours. If any customer sees +10% billed tokens vs preview, roll back immediately.
Ashwin: Adding a gating metric: percent of previewed invoices that match final invoice within 2% — target >= 98% in sample.
Dana: Running the preview now. attaching query I’m using:
Dana: ```sql
-- invoice preview sample
SELECT account_id, SUM(usage_tokens) AS tokens, SUM(estimated_cost) AS est_cost
FROM billing.meter_exports
WHERE account_id IN (SELECT id FROM experiments.sample_50)
GROUP BY account_id;
```
billing-bot: [automated] Invoice preview job started (job_id=inv-prev-1856001).
Marta: Ashwin — can you also stub out a quick alert in Console for any sudden jump in token_rate_per_min > 200% baseline?
Ashwin: On it. I’ll push an alert rule and link it in here when ready.
Ryan: Approvals: I can sign off on finance side if Dana + Ashwin report green. Legal already confirmed T&Cs are covered.
Marta: Thanks. One more: ensure customer-facing emails don’t go out for the canary cohort (this is internal test).
Dana: Confirmed no outbound comms.
billing-bot: [automated] Reconciliation job completed: 50 accounts checked, 1 anomaly flagged (account: 3472, variance 0.8%). Details: /ops/billing/reports/1856001234
Ashwin: I see the anomaly — investigating root cause (likely late refunds).
Marta: Given that only 1/50 is out of threshold and <3 anomalies, this is a green signal. Dana/Ashwin, mark as green and I’ll schedule the canary kickoff for Monday 09:00 PT.
Dana: Green from my side (sample passed manual spot-checks).
Ashwin: Green — alert rule pushed: alert_id=canary-rate-surge-1856.
Ryan: Finance sign-off done. I’ll monitor billing dashboards during rollout.
Marta: Thanks all. Will post the rollout runbook in docs after kickoff. @Ashwin please include rollback playbook snippet. :thumbsup:
Ashwin: Will add rollback commands to runbook. snippet:
Ashwin: ```bash
# rollback canary
./deploy.sh --config=pricing-canary.json --action=rollback --candidates=legacy-exclude
```
Marta: Great. Closing thread — followups can go in the runbook PR.
